svg.text: Figure 2.4. The conditions: where each TILE_CONDITIONS bit is set, the register, and the error line
A. The twelve sources, the set-only register and the error line (§4.13, §6.6, §8.2)
OR over link, eject and C&C FIFOs:
access; a store to a read-only register *
C&C's sticky error bit, a wake for C&C
a store is a bus error (condition 6),
clr to all 11 cells: the clear wins over a set in the same cycle
* A store to TILE_CONDITIONS is a bus error. P: program error. H: hardware-fault detector; no program on a correct design sets it. 6 and 7 can also mean a fault (a corrupted image).
B. One bit cell: set-only, cleared on entering HALT (§4.13)
D = (Q | set) & ¬clr: once set, a bit holds until the tile enters HALT; a set in the clear's cycle is lost (the
clear wins). A bit set while halted (say, a bad mode during loading) holds into RUN, where the loader can check it.
Nothing in RUN clears a bit, so a program cannot hide one.
C. The overflow detector: conditions 1, 2, 3, 5 and 8 (§4.13)
write enable = push & ¬full; set = push & full. The arriving item is dropped on every
overflow. Full is the count before the cycle's pop, so a push at full overflows even with
a pop in the same cycle.
D. What each condition means for the machine
nothing; the tile falls behind its timetable
nothing: the packet lands; the counter stays at 0
the PTR or HIST request (an increment)
halts the tile's controller; engines and router run on
halts the tile's controller; engines and router run on
the packet (mode 0 or 8–15 is always dropped)

• A condition means the software did something wrong, or the hardware is faulty: a correct program on correct hardware reads TILE_CONDITIONS = 0 forever. Setting one stops nothing except 6 and 7, which halt

• Entering HALT (the RUN → HALT edge, or chip reset) clears every bit; HALT → RUN does not. A program finds new conditions in a phase by reading TILE_CONDITIONS at its start and again at its end. C&C learns
at once through the error line, and collects the tiles' bits with REPORT (§6.6, a C&C and software protocol).
• Detectors for 1, 3 and 8 are drawn in the router, read-port and GATHER figures still to come; this figure fixes their set expressions and what they drop.
condition sets, Q and the error line
junction (crossings without a dot don't connect); wedge: clocked register
TILE_CONDITIONS holds 11 set-only bits, one per error a tile can detect; entering HALT clears them all, and the clear wins over a set in the same cycle.
Their OR is the tile's error line to C&C. Five are overflow detectors that drop the arriving item; two (5 and 8) can only mean a hardware fault.
The register is read-only: a store to it is itself a bus error.
